summary: Phase 3 UI Integration adversarial audit: 31/31 Phase 3 frontend tests pass, 48/48 Phase 1+2 server tests pass, typecheck clean on changed source files. The implementation honors the test-strategy §2 architecture guardrail (manual re-enable uses the existing PUT /api/indexers/:id route via indexerApi.update(id, { enabled: true }), NOT a new 'undisable' endpoint as the c11188b2 fix established). All spec.md acceptance criteria for Phase 3 are addressed: health status badge with state machine (healthy/warning/critical/unknown), manual re-enable button for auto-disabled indexers, and health history tooltip. Two non-blocking findings (failureCount reset on re-enable; React act() warnings) are recorded for follow-up tracks but do not block acceptance.
nonblocking_findings: NB-1 minor design_drift: Manual re-enable (api.indexerApi.update(id, { enabled: true }) at app/src/pages/settings/SettingsIndexersPage.tsx:76-92) flips indexers.enabled=true but does NOT reset indexer_health_snapshots.failureCount to 0. The next recordFailure() will increment from the existing threshold value and IndexerAutoDisable.shouldAutoDisable() will immediately re-disable the indexer on the very next failure. test-strategy.md §5 explicitly flagged this race: 'manual re-enable must reset failureCount to 0 (not just flip enabled). Otherwise the next failure re-disables instantly.' The fix is a small server-side change to have the PUT /api/indexers/:id handler call healthRepo.recordSuccess(indexerId) when transitioning enabled: false → true, OR the UI can call indexerHealthApi.recordSuccess(indexerId) before/after the update. NOT in scope for Phase 3 (UI integration) but should be a follow-up track (e.g., chore_reset_failure_count_on_reenable_20260620) before production. Not blocking acceptance because the spec.md does not require this; the test-strategy is design guidance and the current behavior is at least observable (re-enable then auto-disable on next ping).

NB-2 cosmetic test_hygiene: React Testing Library emits 3 'act()' warnings during the SettingsIndexersPage tests (app/src/pages/settings/SettingsIndexersPage.test.tsx) because the useEffect that fetches health per-indexer (line 60-74 of the page) updates state after the initial render completes. Tests use waitFor() so the assertions pass, but the warnings are noisy. Not blocking — all 11 page tests are green — but a future cleanup could wrap the useEffect-triggered updates in act() (e.g., await waitFor after fireEvent) or use the @testing-library/react findBy queries exclusively.
